Délka kroku (m). Kratší krok při stejném: Stride length (m). A shorter stride at the same pace = higher cadence and vice versa. What matters is the change against your baseline in comparable conditions.
Dnešní kapacita = kolik si dnes můžete d: Today's capacity = how much you can afford today so that: (1) the last 7 days don't exceed your weekly capacity — the same one shown in Load (capacity + 15 % margin, adjusted by readiness during the week), (2) this week stays on target for the cycle (90 / 100 / 110 / 55 %), (3) no single run exceeds the capacity of a single run, (4) the total load (heart rate × time from all activities) stays below the ceiling. The strictest of them applies — each channel shows which. When mechanics are above the threshold of 25, today shrinks further (volume −20 %, intensity and descent by half); when load is above the threshold, a recovery week follows. That way both axes stay below the threshold.
Doba kontaktu se zemí (ms) — jak dlouho: Ground contact time (ms) — how long the foot is on the ground. An increase against your baseline (at a comparable pace) suggests fatigue or loss of support.
Doba spánku a jeho efektivita. Vztahujem: Sleep duration and efficiency. We relate it to your usual amount — an accumulated sleep debt lowers tolerance to load and impairs recovery.
Efektivní „plochý ekvivalent\" kilometrů: Effective “flat-equivalent” kilometres over 7 days — distance adjusted for the energy cost of the gradient (Minetti). A hilly run costs more than an equally long flat one, so this number is higher than the real km on rolling terrain. For a jump in load, the Sensitive engine counts terrain cost separately: ascent by energy cost, descent by eccentric load — a steep downhill costs less energy but loads the legs more.
Jak jednotvárná byla zátěž v týdnu (vyso: How monotonous the load was during the week (high = almost the same every day, no rest day). High monotony + high volume = “strain”, linked to overload. Ideally alternate hard and easy days.
Kadence — počet kroků za minutu. Pokles: Cadence — steps per minute. A drop in cadence at the same pace often comes with fatigue. There's no single right number; what matters is stability against your norm.
Kilometry naběhané v klesání od −5 % skl: Kilometres run downhill steeper than −5 % over 7 days. Descent loads the muscles eccentrically (braking) more than its low metabolic cost suggests — so we track it separately. A sharp rise often triggers thigh and knee pain.
Klidový tep přes noc. Trvale zvýšený pro: Overnight resting heart rate. Persistently raised against your baseline = the body hasn't recovered (fatigue, stress, illness). A one-off swing doesn't matter; watch the trend.
Kolik z vaší zátěže tvoří tvrdé/rychlé b: How much of your load comes from hard/fast runs over 7 days against your norm. An increase in hard sessions raises the risk more than extra kilometres at an easy pace. Interpret it by how much intensity you usually tolerate.
Kvalita spánku = podíl hlubokého a REM s: Sleep quality = the share of deep and REM sleep in total sleep, and efficiency (time asleep / time in bed), a 7-night average against your 8-week norm. Deep sleep mainly serves physical recovery, REM the recovery of the nervous system. When the share or efficiency is clearly below your norm, today's readiness goes down — even if you slept long enough. Watches only estimate sleep stages, so quality carries at most half the weight of a signal.
Nametrážované klesání (sbíhání) za 7 dní: Measured descent (downhill running) over 7 days in metres. Descent loads the muscles eccentrically more than the flat — so we track it separately. Compare it with “usually”: a sharp jump often triggers knee/thigh pain.
Nejtěžší jednotlivý trénink vůči vašemu: The hardest single session against your maximum over the last 30 days — by distance and by intensity (the worse of the two counts). One run clearly bigger than you're used to is the strongest trigger of overload.
Odhad délky nejdelšího běhu, který teď z: An estimate of the longest run you can manage now without a big jump in load — derived from your recent history. It serves as a ceiling for planning the weekend long run.
Podíl doby kontaktu se zemí na celkové d: The share of ground contact time in the whole stride (duty factor). Lower tends to be a springier, more economical run. It's judged against your baseline at a comparable pace — an increase comes with fatigue.
Poměr posledních 7 dní ku vašemu 28denní: The ratio of the last 7 days to your 28-day average. Around ×1.0 means you're running as usual. Well above ×1.3 = a fast increase (riskier); below ×0.8 = easing off or a break. For runners we treat it only as context, not as the main warning.
Poměr vertikálního pohybu k délce kroku: The ratio of vertical movement to stride length (%). Lower = a more economical, “flatter” run. What matters is the shift against your baseline at a comparable pace and terrain — a worsening is often a sign of fatigue in your form.
Relativní úsilí porovná tepovou zátěž bě: Relative effort compares a run's heart-rate load with your runs of the last 8 weeks (below / usual / above / well above usual). ‘Heart rate at pace’ shows how much higher or lower your heart rate was than you usually need for the same pace — a clearly higher heart rate at an easy pace is often a sign of fatigue, heat or illness.
Skóre stavu (0–100): čím vyšší, tím lépe: State score (0–100): the higher, the better. It's 100 minus the risk made up of mechanics, load and symptoms, weighted by the strength of the evidence. 100 = nothing to watch. Above 60 is low risk, 31 to 60 watch, 30 and below high risk. When a safety rule, recurring pain or the load state moves a day into a higher band, its place in the band is set by their severity together with the model. On ordinary days the display brings out even small differences. For each signal we show how many percentage points it takes off the Score. Always against your own history.
Součet tréninkové zátěže (běh i jiný spo: The sum of training load (running and other sports) over the last 7 days in load units. The further above your usual week, the bigger the acute load. Watch mainly the jump against previous weeks, not the absolute number.
Souhrn stability běžecké formy v čase. K: A summary of how stable your running form is over time. A falling curve = form is breaking down (typically fatigue); stable = you're holding your technique.
Spolehlivost — nakolik je už postavená v: Reliability — how far your baseline is built (number of comparable sessions and days of history). While it's low, mechanics signals are better not shown so they don't confuse.
Symetrie doby kontaktu levá/pravá (%). I: Left/right ground contact time balance (%). Ideally around 50/50. A growing imbalance may relate to one-sided overload — watch the trend, not a single run.
Variabilita tepové frekvence přes noc (m: Overnight heart rate variability (ms). Higher = better recovered. What matters is the deviation from YOUR baseline (in per cent), not the absolute value — a clearer drop against your usual spread suggests fatigue or an oncoming illness.
Vertikální oscilace — o kolik se při kaž: Vertical oscillation — how much you “bounce” with each step (cm). Lower tends to be more economical. It's judged against your own runs, not against tables.
